🌟 Today’s Tibetan Adventure!

Today, we are going to learn how to ask "What is this?" in Tibetan, and how to point to things and name them—like saying "This is a book!" or "This is not a pen!"
The Magic Sandwich Rule 🥪 Making a sentence in Tibetan is just like making a sandwich! Top Bread: Start with འདི། (di = this) or འདི་ཚོ། (di-tso = these). Yummy Middle: Put the Question ག་རེ་ or Name / Noun in the middle. Bottom Bread: Always end with རེད། (re = is / are) or མ་རེད། (ma-re = is not / are not) Let's Try It! Questions: འདི་ ག་རེ་ རེད། — What is this? འདི་ཚོ་ ག་རེ་ རེད། — What are these? Answers: འདི་ ཁང་པ་ རེད། — This is a house. འདི་ཚོ་ ཁང་པ་ རེད། — These are houses.

འདི་ ཁང་པ་ མ་རེད། — This is not a house. འདི་ཚོ་ ཁང་པ་ མ་རེད། — These are not houses.

Fun Tip: In Tibetan, nouns never change their form, there’s no plural ending like adding an "s" in English (e.g., house to houses)!! Whether you have 1 house or 100, the noun itself stays exactly the same (e.g., ཁང་པ་ stays ཁང་པ་).
